question: Can the Fish Ark Southern Luzon photoguide provide a reusable, site-aware source for freshwater fish coverage across the named survey areas?

findings.sourceType: official DOST-PCAARRD program article; summary only
findings.publicationAsReported: UPLB photoguide on diminutive native freshwater fish; article does not give the guidebook title or a downloadable copy.

namedStudyAreas: Mt. Makiling Forest Reserve rivers and streams
surveySummaryAsReported.voucherStatement: Some collection voucher specimens were reportedly deposited at the UPLB Research Station and Museum of Natural History; no accession numbers are provided.

findings.access: The official PCAARRD article was read. It summarizes the guide's reported scope but contains no 72-name list, individual site list, dates, station-to-taxon assignments or voucher accessions. No guidebook download was located in this review.
findings.interpretation: This is a high-value source-access lead because the described survey spans multiple freshwater areas in Southern Luzon. The 72-species and 28-site totals are article-reported aggregates, not a verified checklist or evidence that each named region, lake or river has a particular species. The named areas are too broad to attach the report to individual waterbody scope units.

findings.sourceType: official UPLB Knowledge Digital Repository catalog metadata
findings.publicationAsReported: Ocampo, Paolo P. (2011). Fish Ark Philippines: Direction for the conservation of native and endemic Philippine freshwater fishers. Terminal report.
findings.access: The repository record confirms author, year, language and document type and explicitly says the document is not currently available there. The full report was not retrieved.
findings.interpretation: This is a related project-report access lead. Its title and document type do not establish that it is the photoguide or the source of the article's 72-species list; treat it as a separate item until that relationship is documented.

findings.sourceType: official DOST STII bibliography record; citation-only lead
findings.publicationAsReported: UPLB Limnological Research Station. 2011. Freshwater Fishes of Southern Luzon, Philippines. University of the Philippines Los Baños, College, Laguna. 91 p.
findings.access: The December 2018 SPHERES issue was identified as the bibliography source during prior source screening. Its current PDF link redirected to a DOST STII URL that this review environment could not retrieve, so the bibliography text was not re-read in this turn. No publication copy was obtained.
findings.interpretation: This citation may identify the photoguide summarized by PCAARRD, but that bibliographic relationship is unconfirmed. Do not merge it with the terminal report or infer its contents from the citation.

evidenceBoundary: The 72-species count, 28-site count and three-year duration are reported by the official PCAARRD summary; the guide and complete underlying inventory were not inspected.
The article names broad study areas but gives no exact 28-site roster, survey dates, methods by site, taxon-by-site table, or link between names and individual lakes, rivers, streams or waterfalls.
The voucher statement covers only some collections and supplies no accession numbers or specimen crosswalk.
The Fish Ark terminal report and the 91-page 2011 bibliography item are separate records; their relationship to the PCAARRD-described photoguide remains unverified.
No species assertion, occurrence, waterbody geometry, current-presence claim, diet, bait, safety or legal statement was added.
No source was attached to a waterbody scope entry because no site-level crosswalk was established.
No item-specific reuse license or public-app publication approval was verified. No external request was sent.

disposition.reason: The official summary makes this a high-value retrieval lead, but the photoguide, exact site roster, taxon list, specimen crosswalk and reuse terms were not available for verification.

nextAction: Through an authorized UPLB Limnological Research Station or Museum of Natural History route, seek the photoguide and exact 28-site roster, methods and field dates, site-to-taxon table, voucher accession crosswalk, distinction from the 2011 terminal report, and item-specific reuse terms. Review candidate names and localities individually before linking any claim to a waterbody scope unit.

sources.supports: Official program article's reported 72-species photoguide, 28 sites, three-year survey, broad study areas and partial voucher-deposit statement.
UPLB repository metadata for Paolo P. Ocampo's 2011 Fish Ark terminal report and the notice that the document is not currently available there.
Official DOST bibliography lead for UPLB Limnological Research Station's 2011 Freshwater Fishes of Southern Luzon citation; current endpoint was not retrievable during this review.
